summary: Private deployment: corporate TLS inspection stripping SNI causes certificate mismatch and intermittent model downloads
description:
Issue summary:
Customer's private deployment (Acme Analytics, private tier) reports intermittent failures when the agent attempts to download model artifacts and make downstream HTTPS calls to model-registry.redwood-internal.net. DNS resolution succeeds for all requests, but TLS handshakes sometimes fail with certificate name mismatch or the client aborts during ServerHello. Small API calls (token checks, pings) usually succeed; large model downloads fail ~30% of the time.

Impact:
- Model pulls for new containers occasionally fail causing model startup retries and longer cold-starts for customers.
- Streaming inference for long responses sometimes resets mid-stream when the model endpoint is reloaded.

Environment:
- Private deployment (on-customer VPC) with VPC endpoint to Redwood's model-registry, routing through corporate perimeter firewall performing TLS inspection.
- Region: us-west-2
- Agent version: 1.12.0
- Serving runtime: rwd-svc-2026-02

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model pull via the Console or run a job that requires a cold-start for redwood-open-7B-v1.
2) Observe logs in agent (agent.log) and attempt manual curl from a jump host inside the same VPC: curl -v https://model-registry.redwood-internal.net/v1/models
3) Repeatedly issue downloads; intermittent failures observed.

Observed behavior:
- DNS returns correct A records consistently.
- curl -v shows TCP handshake completes, but in failing cases the ClientHello seen by the server lacks an SNI extension (verified via tcpdump on customer network).
- Server returns default certificate (CN does not match expected host) causing client certificate name mismatch error.
- When SNI is present (successful TLS handshakes), connections proceed normally.
- Agent logs: "tls: server certificate does not match expected name" or "handshake aborted by peer" on failing attempts.

Expected behavior:
- TLS ClientHello includes SNI with model-registry.redwood-internal.net and server presents correct certificate for that name, allowing handshake to complete consistently.

Logs / Evidence attached by customer:
- tcpdump (pcap) showing alternating ClientHello packets: some contain SNI extension, some do not.
- curl -v outputs for success and failure cases.
- Agent logs excerpt and model-pull stack traces.

Investigation notes (Support):
- Reproduced handshake mismatch in our lab by removing SNI from ClientHello; server returns default vhost certificate and client fails verification.
- Hypothesis: Corporate TLS inspection appliance (explicit TLS proxy) is either stripping or rewriting the SNI extension when proxying outbound TLS flows, or it is performing a re-encapsulation without preserving the original SNI. This results in the backend load balancer selecting the default certificate.
- Intermittent nature explained by: appliance is stateful and some flows are proxied differently based on session affinity or connection reuse; some agent processes reuse connections that already had SNI preserved.
- Confirmed no rate-limiting or 5xx on Redwood side for these requests during captured windows.

Suggested actions / Workaround:
- Short term: Customer's firewall team to configure TLS inspection to preserve SNI for hosts matching *.redwood-internal.net or create an allowlist so TLS bypass is performed for model-registry endpoints.
- Alternative: Configure the agent to use an internal HTTP proxy that performs TLS passthrough (no MITM) for registry hosts. Agent supports an explicit PROXY env to route only model pulls.
- Customer has provided corporate firewall logs and agreed to test an allowlist.

Next steps / Requested from customer:
1) Firewall/proxy team to confirm whether SNI rewriting/stripping is enabled and test an allowlist bypass for model-registry.redwood-internal.net.
2) Provide an additional pcap after bypass is applied to verify SNI is present in all ClientHello packets.
3) If bypass not possible, confirm whether corporate CA is being injected and whether the agent runtime trusts that CA (note: trusting injected CAs weakens security; preferred solution is bypass for known Redwood endpoints).

Resolution notes:
- Pending customer firewall change. Support has documented exact hostnames and IP ranges to allow. If customer applies the allowlist and problem persists, escalate to Networking Eng (linked INT-1142) and provide fresh pcaps.

References:
- Internal TLS Inspection runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/9842/TLS+Inspection+Runbook
- Related GH issue updating agent proxy handling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-tools/pull/342
